rules.assign_group_help: Whoever in the group holds the fewest open reports and can see this one.

crowd.title: Crowd moderation
crowd.help: When enough trusted members report a post within a few hours, it is hidden (or sent back to approval) until a moderator reviews it in the report centre. The author is told why. Restoring it is one click, and counts against the people who reported it.
crowd.threshold_help: How many members it takes (at least 2). With trust on, a member counts for between 0.5 and 1.5 by their record, so this is a total weight.
crowd.window_help: Only reports from this many hours count.
crowd.action_help: A first post hides (or holds back) its whole discussion.
crowd.min_age_help: Reports from newer accounts don't count, so new accounts can't brigade.
crowd.min_posts_help: Reports from members with fewer posts don't count.
crowd.trust_help: Members whose reports were upheld count for more, members whose reports were rejected or restored count for less. New reporters count as one.
crowd.address_help: Reports sent from one connection (an IPv4 address, or an IPv6 /64) count once, as do accounts an alt-account extension links. The addresses are stored only as a keyed hash.
crowd.exempt_help: Staff (anyone who can see flags or hide posts) are always exempt: reports about their posts are left for you.
crowd.cooldown_help: A post staff restored isn't hidden by reports again for this long.
crowd.tags_help: A different number for a tag: empty for the setting above, 0 for never. A discussion with several tags uses the highest; one with a 0 is never hidden. A queue's own threshold beats these.
